headline_hook: Anthropic Files Its S-1, OpenAI Ships to AWS, and Someone Hacked Instagram by Asking Nicely
preview_topics: AI agents as the new attack surface

pick_of_the_day.thesis: When your AI support agent IS the security vulnerability, traditional threat models break down — every company rushing to deploy customer-facing AI agents just got a live preview of what happens when the attack surface is a conversation.

model_literacy.relevance: Today's Meta AI hack and Claude Code supply chain attack stories both exploit the same root cause: AI systems that can't distinguish trusted instructions from adversarial input. Understanding the taxonomy — direct injection, indirect injection, social engineering of AI agents — is essential as agents gain real-world permissions.

items.title: Anthropic Confidentially Files S-1 — the IPO Clock Starts
items.angle: The first frontier AI lab to file for an IPO signals that Anthropic believes its revenue trajectory can survive public-market scrutiny — and sets the valuation benchmark every other AI company will be measured against.
items.key_fact: Confidential S-1 filed with the SEC

items.title: Hackers Social-Engineered Meta's AI Into Handing Over Instagram Accounts
items.angle: No exploits, no zero-days — attackers just asked Meta's AI support agent nicely and got access to high-profile accounts. This is the most concrete proof yet that deployed AI agents are a novel attack surface.
items.key_fact: AI support agent granted account access via persuasive prompts alone

items.title: Open and Closed Models Are Scaling on Different Exponentials
items.angle: Interconnects frames the open-vs-closed debate not as a quality gap but as two fundamentally different value curves — essential reading for anyone choosing their model strategy.
items.key_fact: Marginal intelligence gains drive value differently across open and closed ecosystems

items.title: Florida Sues OpenAI Over AI Safety Risks
items.angle: A state-level lawsuit against OpenAI could set precedent for how US states regulate AI independently of federal action — watch for copycat filings.
items.key_fact: First major US state lawsuit targeting a frontier AI lab directly

items.title: OpenAI Models and Codex Go GA on Amazon Bedrock
items.angle: OpenAI shipping through AWS means enterprises can now access GPT and Codex inside their existing security and compliance stack — the cloud-provider model-hosting war just escalated.
items.key_fact: Generally available on AWS with full Bedrock governance integration

items.title: NVIDIA Drops Cosmos 3 — Fully Open Omnimodel for Physical AI
items.angle: The first fully open model with native video, image, and robot action understanding — NVIDIA's open-source counterweight to the proprietary robotics AI push.
items.key_fact: Handles video, images, and robot actions in a single open model

items.title: JetBrains Releases Mellum2: A 12B MoE Model Built for IDEs
items.angle: The IDE maker building its own brain — purpose-built for code understanding with Kotlin/Java-first priorities that generic models can't match.

items.title: OpenAI Demos a Voice-First Agentic Mobile OS
items.angle: Users talk, agents act across the entire phone — OpenAI is building toward an OS-level AI layer, not just another app.
items.key_fact: Voice-first mobile OS with cross-app agent capabilities

items.title: Anthropic Resets All Pro and Max Rate Limits
items.angle: If Claude Code has been throttling you, your limits are fresh — Anthropic also fixed the bug causing premature limit hits.
items.key_fact: 5-hour and weekly limits reset for all Pro and Max users

items.title: Codex Python SDK Turns Codex Into a Programmable Building Block
items.angle: Embed Codex directly in Python apps — threads, streaming, image input, sandbox control. Codex just became an API, not just a product.
items.key_fact: Full programmatic control: threads, turns, streaming, resume, sandbox access

items.title: OpenAI Python SDK v2.40.0 Adds Native Bedrock Responses Support
items.angle: The SDK-level integration that makes today's OpenAI-on-AWS announcement immediately usable — both Python and Node covered.
items.key_fact: Native Bedrock Responses support in official SDKs

items.title: How Google Used Gemini to Build I/O 2026
items.angle: A rare behind-the-scenes look at how a frontier lab dogfoods its own model at scale — from content creation to technical demos.
items.key_fact: Gemini used across Google's I/O production pipeline

items.title: Stanford CS336 Ships Official CLAUDE.md Guidelines for AI Agent Use
items.angle: A top CS program codifying what AI agents can and can't do on assignments — this will be the template other universities copy.
items.key_fact: Rules for AI agent scope, citation, and academic integrity in coursework

items.title: Qwen3.5 Trained With Agentic RL Matches GPT-5.5 in Tool Use
items.angle: Post-training on real MCP-server-based agentic RL environments teaches general tool-use capabilities that transfer to unseen benchmarks — not just benchmark tricks.
items.key_fact: Qwen3.5-122B matches GPT-5.5 on tool-use tasks after agentic RL

items.title: Why Video Agent Models Are Next — Inside xAI's Grok Imagine
items.angle: The engineer who built Grok Imagine in 3 months explains why video agents are the next frontier and why video generation vs. world models is the wrong dichotomy.
items.key_fact: Grok Imagine built in 3 months; video agents framed as the next capability frontier

items.title: IBM Research: Enterprise AI Is Bottlenecked by Agent Logic, Not Model Capability
items.angle: The missing piece isn't smarter models — it's the orchestration, memory, and decision-making layers that make AI reliable at enterprise scale.
items.key_fact: Agent logic (orchestration, memory, decisions) identified as the enterprise adoption bottleneck

items.title: LangGraph 1.2.3 Adds Named Subagents and v3 Streaming
items.angle: Named tool-dispatched subagents make multi-agent orchestration observable and debuggable — the subagent naming alone is worth the update.
items.key_fact: v3 streaming support for RemoteGraph plus named subagent dispatch

items.title: ai-rules-sync: One Config File to Rule All Your AI Coding Agents
items.angle: Syncs CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, Copilot, and Windsurf configs from a single source — zero dependencies, solves the multi-tool config drift problem.
items.key_fact: Supports 7 AI coding tools from one source of truth

quick_links.angle: Malicious SessionStart hooks and VS Code task injection — AI dev tooling attack vectors are real
quick_links.key_fact: Specific attack vectors in Claude Code settings.json and VS Code tasks

quick_links.angle: The vision-to-shipping gap collapsed in 16 months — anyone can build now
quick_links.key_fact: PewDiePie's AI suite hit #1 on HN with 10K+ stars

quick_links.title: Mollick: The AI Usefulness Debate Is Over, Now It's About Organizational Scaling
quick_links.angle: Enterprise leaders confirm real value — the question is individual-to-firm transformation
quick_links.key_fact: Adoption inflection point: from 'does it work' to 'how do we scale it'
